item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-bad659f1529f32b5","start_unit":16,"end_unit":17,"fact_summary":"On 10 February 2023, FARDC handed MONUSCO seven children who had escaped the ADF after being held for three weeks at the FARDC intelligence office in Beni; MONUSCO had advocated for their transfer for psychosocial care and reintegration.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.7","6B.6"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly within 2023; concerns an event preceding the handover and the resulting protection response.","ruler_attribution":"The source attributes the detention to FARDC and the advocacy and reintegration response to MONUSCO; it does not attribute a personal decision to Tshisekedi.","limitations":["The source does not identify Tshisekedi's direct involvement or explain whether the three-week detention complied with law."]},{"source_id":"SRC-bad659f1529f32b5","start_unit":17,"end_unit":17,"fact_summary":"Since 2018, MONUSCO advocacy with armed groups in North Kivu produced unilateral declarations and roadmaps against child recruitment; the UN reports that hundreds of children subsequently left armed groups in the Beni-Butembo-Lubero region.","question_ids":["3B.7","6B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The reported process spans 2018 onward and includes results during the target period.","ruler_attribution":"The source attributes the declarations and advocacy to MONUSCO and armed groups, not to Tshisekedi personally.","limitations":["No direct presidential role or government funding/enforcement is established."]},{"source_id":"SRC-94baeafc401ac407","start_unit":2,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"In 2023, the DRC held presidential, legislative, and provincial elections amid deteriorating eastern security and heightened humanitarian pressure; by year-end 6.8 million people were internally displaced and more than 500,000 refugees and asylum seekers were hosted, while inflation was expected above 19% and the Congolese franc had depreciated by more than 28%.","question_ids":["2B.10","3B.6","3B.10","5B.9","6B.6","6B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly reports 2023 conditions and results.","ruler_attribution":"The source describes national conditions during Tshisekedi's presidency but does not assign causation for each indicator to him.","limitations":["The figures are national outcomes with multiple causes and do not isolate presidential responsibility."]},{"source_id":"SRC-94baeafc401ac407","start_unit":2,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"The government continued implementing the Programme de Développement des 145 Territoires (PDL-145T), intended to expand basic social services, improve local resilience, and strengthen local public institutions.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.6","6B.1","6B.2","6B.9","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The source reports implementation during 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The source attributes the programme to the Government of the DRC and identifies it as a national priority under Tshisekedi's administration.","limitations":["This passage does not provide executed expenditure, completion rates, or independent outcome verification."]},{"source_id":"SRC-94baeafc401ac407","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"The UN reported that its technical, logistical, communications, and early-warning support helped the 2023 elections occur within constitutional deadlines while minimizing risks of crisis and preventing conflict.","question_ids":["2B.7","4B.1","4B.10","8B.5","8B.9"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Directly concerns the 2023 electoral process.","ruler_attribution":"The source attributes the support to the UN system in cooperation with state institutions; it does not establish that Tshisekedi personally directed these measures.","limitations":["The statement is a UN self-assessment and does not independently assess electoral fairness or disputed results."]},{"source_id":"SRC-94baeafc401ac407","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"The government pursued universal health coverage measures including free maternity care, free newborn care, family planning, free education, and continuity of schooling for displaced children, with UN support.","question_ids":["6B.1","6B.2","6B.3","6B.6","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The source reports these actions as part of 2023 implementation.","ruler_attribution":"The source attributes the measures to the government and identifies UN cooperation; it does not specify Tshisekedi's personal directive or the level of execution.","limitations":["No uptake, coverage, funding, quality, or distribution data are provided."]},{"source_id":"SRC-94baeafc401ac407","start_unit":2,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"On 21 November 2023, the DRC government and the UN signed a joint disengagement plan for MONUSCO withdrawal, and the UN began planning transition arrangements to preserve civilian-protection, disarmament, security-sector-reform, justice, and criminal-chain capacities.","question_ids":["2B.7","3B.9","3B.10","8B.9","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly concerns a formal 2023 agreement and transition planning.","ruler_attribution":"The plan is attributed jointly to the DRC government and the UN; the source does not identify Tshisekedi's specific negotiating choices.","limitations":["The passage describes planning rather than completed withdrawal outcomes or durable capacity."]},{"source_id":"SRC-03ff5e3fa4e31a59","start_unit":1,"end_unit":1,"fact_summary":"In a December 2023 campaign speech in Butembo, Tshisekedi said his government had supported FARDC, cooperated militarily with Uganda against the ADF in Beni, and created an Armed Defence Reserve to train and supervise Wazalendo fighters.","question_ids":["2B.2","2B.5","2B.8","3B.2","8B.1","8B.2","8B.3","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly reports Tshisekedi's stated 2023 security strategy.","ruler_attribution":"The claims and policy commitments are directly attributed to Tshisekedi.","limitations":["The article does not independently verify implementation, legal safeguards, or effects of the reserve and allied operations."]},{"source_id":"SRC-03ff5e3fa4e31a59","start_unit":2,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"Tshisekedi claimed credit for instituting free primary education and free maternity care, and promised to extend free education to secondary schools if reelected.","question_ids":["6B.1","6B.2","8B.1","8B.6"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The claims and promise were made in December 2023 and refer partly to the preceding term.","ruler_attribution":"The claims and promise are directly attributed to Tshisekedi.","limitations":["The source provides anecdotal confirmation and no national implementation or outcome audit."]},{"source_id":"SRC-03ff5e3fa4e31a59","start_unit":2,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"Tshisekedi presented the PDL-145T as rebuilding territorial administrative offices, schools, health centres, roads, ports, and airports, creating youth employment, and supporting agriculture; the article includes local witnesses who reported seeing schools and health centres built in parts of Lubero and Beni.","question_ids":["5B.6","6B.2","8B.2","8B.6","8B.7"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Directly concerns the programme's reported 2023 implementation and claimed local results.","ruler_attribution":"The programme claims are attributed to Tshisekedi; local observations are attributed to interviewed residents.","limitations":["The article does not provide project counts, budgets, completion dates, or independent verification."]},{"source_id":"SRC-03ff5e3fa4e31a59","start_unit":2,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"Tshisekedi stated that his economic strategy prioritized agricultural production and domestic processing of minerals, including encouraging battery factories and industrial zones in the DRC; he cited a national industrialization master plan developed by Industry Minister Julien Paluku.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.4","5B.6","8B.1","8B.2"],"polarity":"context","period_fit":"Directly reports a December 2023 campaign programme and claimed institutional planning.","ruler_attribution":"The strategy is attributed to Tshisekedi and the industrial plan to Minister Paluku.","limitations":["The source reports policy intentions and a plan, not executed budgets, enforcement, or measurable outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-14f529ed1eca94ea","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"Human Rights Watch reported that authorities cracked down on opposition members and media before the December 2023 election, while martial law had not curbed widespread armed-group violence; government forces killed dozens of civilians during an August 30 operation enforcing a demonstration ban in Goma.","question_ids":["3B.5","3B.6","3B.8","3B.9","4B.3","4B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly reports events and conditions during 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The abuses are attributed to Congolese authorities and government forces during Tshisekedi's administration; the source does not establish his personal order for the operation.","limitations":["The source does not resolve the full chain of command or distinguish all security units involved."]},{"source_id":"SRC-14f529ed1eca94ea","start_unit":4,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"In 2023, authorities arrested satirical comedian Junior Nkole for a video deemed insulting to the president, opposition member Lens Omelonga over criticism of the first lady's foundation, opposition adviser Salomon Kalonda on treason allegations, and presidential candidate Franck Diongo on a weapons allegation; Diongo was later released without charge.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.3","3B.5","3B.8","4B.3","4B.9","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly reports arrests and detention during 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The arrests are attributed to government security, intelligence, military-intelligence, and Republican Guard personnel; the source does not prove Tshisekedi personally ordered them.","limitations":["The legal merits of the individual allegations were not adjudicated in this source."]},{"source_id":"SRC-14f529ed1eca94ea","start_unit":5,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"On 8 September 2023, police arrested journalist Stanis Bujakera, who remained detained and faced forgery and false-information charges over an intelligence note attributed to an article that did not bear his name; the arrest generated international criticism.","question_ids":["3B.8","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","7B.2","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly concerns a 2023 arrest and detention.","ruler_attribution":"The arrest and charges are attributed to Congolese authorities; no personal presidential order is shown.","limitations":["The source does not report the final judicial disposition by the end of 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-14f529ed1eca94ea","start_unit":6,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"Human Rights Watch reported that more than 100 armed groups remained active in eastern DRC; Kivu Security Tracker recorded at least 1,211 civilians killed in Ituri between January and October 2023, including at least 80 killed by Congolese security forces, while surrendered Mobondo fighters were sent to military training without vetting for prior abuses.","question_ids":["2B.4","2B.5","2B.9","3B.2","3B.6","3B.7","3B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly reports 2023 violence, security-force conduct, and integration practice.","ruler_attribution":"The source attributes the killings and recruitment practice to Congolese security institutions and government policy, without identifying Tshisekedi's personal involvement.","limitations":["The aggregate death count includes unidentified armed actors and does not establish presidential causation."]},{"source_id":"SRC-14f529ed1eca94ea","start_unit":7,"end_unit":8,"fact_summary":"The Tshisekedi administration reaffirmed commitment to transitional justice but had taken no concrete steps to advance domestic justice; in June the government requested an ICC investigation into increased violence and abuses in North Kivu and signed a cooperation memorandum with the ICC prosecutor.","question_ids":["2B.9","3B.4","3B.10","7B.6","7B.7","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly concerns government actions and omissions during 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The administration's position and the ICC request are attributed to the Tshisekedi government.","limitations":["The source does not assess whether the ICC cooperation produced results during the target period."]},{"source_id":"SRC-14f529ed1eca94ea","start_unit":7,"end_unit":8,"fact_summary":"In late September 2023, Tshisekedi requested an accelerated MONUSCO withdrawal by the end of 2023, arguing that peacekeeping missions deployed for 25 years had failed to address rebellions and armed conflict.","question_ids":["2B.7","2B.10","3B.9","8B.1","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly reports a 2023 presidential request and stated rationale.","ruler_attribution":"The request and rationale are directly attributed to Tshisekedi.","limitations":["The source does not establish whether the accelerated timetable was implemented or its effects on civilian protection."]},{"source_id":"SRC-8833adb399a7e84d","start_unit":3,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"Amnesty International and IBGDH reported that industrial cobalt and copper mining around Kolwezi involved forced evictions, inadequate consultation, inadequate compensation, destruction of homes and crops, beatings, sexual assault, and lack of effective grievance or remedy mechanisms; the report urged DRC authorities to end forced evictions and strengthen enforcement.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.7","5B.4","5B.5","5B.8","6B.3","6B.7","7B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The report was published in September 2023 but much of the documented conduct occurred in earlier years; it is relevant as a 2023 institutional finding about ongoing accountability and safeguards.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes failures to mining companies, state mining interests, government authorities, police, and military personnel; it calls on President Tshisekedi and DRC authorities but does not prove his personal direction.","limitations":["The field research focused on six projects and relied on interviews and documentary evidence; the report does not quantify Tshisekedi's direct involvement."]},{"source_id":"SRC-cc8e936cb0298b65","start_unit":5,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"ACLED reported that government forces often suppressed opposition gatherings during Tshisekedi's term; between January 2019 and November 2023, demonstrations averaged fewer than 45 events per month, and security forces blocked or stopped political gatherings, including an opposition attempt to assemble outside CENI offices on 25 May 2023.","question_ids":["4B.3","4B.9","8B.5","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The source reports a 2019-2023 pattern and a specific May 2023 event.","ruler_attribution":"The conduct is attributed to government forces during Tshisekedi's term; the source does not identify a personal presidential order.","limitations":["The demonstration average is descriptive and does not by itself establish whether every restriction was unlawful."]},{"source_id":"SRC-cc8e936cb0298b65","start_unit":5,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"ACLED reported concerns that CENI was politically close to the government, that its leadership and procedures were controversial, and that selection of Denis Kadima—described by critics as close to Tshisekedi—triggered widespread demonstrations; CENI also faced logistical problems with voting machines, ballots, and the electoral roll.","question_ids":["4B.1","4B.2","4B.4","4B.10","8B.2","8B.5"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The institutional findings concern the electoral process leading into the 2023 election, with some background dating to 2020-2021.","ruler_attribution":"The perceived closeness is attributed to critics and ACLED's reporting; the source does not prove Tshisekedi personally selected Kadima or directed CENI operations.","limitations":["These are concerns and perceptions reported by ACLED, not a final judicial finding of electoral capture."]},{"source_id":"SRC-cc8e936cb0298b65","start_unit":6,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"ACLED recorded 15 targeted political-violence events in 2021, 19 in 2022, and 32 by December 2023; at least 10 political parties were targeted in 2023, and UDPS supporters were both the most targeted group and the most active in violence against other political groups since 2019.","question_ids":["3B.3","3B.8","4B.3","4B.7","4B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly reports trends through the 2023 election period.","ruler_attribution":"The data concern political actors including the ruling UDPS, but do not establish that Tshisekedi personally ordered or participated in the violence.","limitations":["The dataset records events and affiliations, not individual responsibility or command relationships."]},{"source_id":"SRC-e8b6fb6c02f2a4d0","start_unit":4,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"On 27 December 2023, opposition candidates and protesters demanded a rerun of the presidential election; police said they used only tear gas, while AP journalists observed physical assaults, and the government had banned the planned protest.","question_ids":["3B.8","4B.1","4B.3","4B.9","4B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly concerns post-election events in December 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The protest ban and police conduct are attributed to the government and police; the report does not identify a personal Tshisekedi order.","limitations":["The allegation that live ammunition was used could not be verified; the article reports conflicting accounts."]},{"source_id":"SRC-e8b6fb6c02f2a4d0","start_unit":4,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"Rights groups and international observers questioned the credibility of the December 2023 election: more than 27% of sampled polling stations reportedly did not open, 152 reports of violence or confrontations were recorded, voting continued in some areas five days after election day, and polling materials were missing or defective.","question_ids":["4B.1","4B.2","4B.4","4B.6","4B.10","7B.1"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly concerns the December 2023 election.","ruler_attribution":"The reported irregularities concern the electoral process under Tshisekedi's administration; the source does not establish his personal responsibility for each failure.","limitations":["The 27% figure derives from a sample of 1,185 observer reports, not all polling stations."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":["SRC-82c83fad0d184a9a","SRC-b410f3198638b3ee","SRC-f6538113cfca1448"],"batch_limitations":["Several supplied documents concern 2025 or 2026 rather than the 2023-2023 target period and were therefore recorded as having no material target-period fact.","The supplied evidence often describes government institutions, security forces, armed groups, or international organizations rather than Tshisekedi's personal decisions; attribution is limited accordingly."]}
